title: Solar panel install
use_case: Solar panel installation: a solar module (1000 x 600 mm, 35 mm thick, 8 kg) waits on its stand beside the two mounting rails. Lift it onto the rails and set it down against the rail end stops (within 5 mm), then start the clamp nut (13 mm hex) at the middle of its long edge on its thread and tighten it to 6 N m.
headline: A tool-change sequence completes the task in 7 of 8 runs.

plan.title: Solar panel installation
plan.description: Lift the solar panel onto its mounting rails and seat it against the end stops, then insert the clamp nut to the thread start and tighten it to 6 N m.
assumptions: Start gap between panel and rail stops is 0 mm.

steps.description: Lift the solar panel onto the mounting rails and set it down against the end stops.
caveats: Suction is an approximation: the seal is a geometric test gating a capped adhesion force; no air flow, leak rate or porosity.

The clamp is an approximation: a 13 mm hex modelled 15 mm tall so the simulated socket can seat (a standard M8 nut is 6.8 mm tall), on a helical joint with a torque ramp; it does not press the panel. The panel is a rigid slab.

steps.description: Insert the clamp nut onto its thread start.
caveats: The clamp is an approximation: a 13 mm hex modelled 15 mm tall so the simulated socket can seat (a standard M8 nut is 6.8 mm tall), on a helical joint with a torque ramp; it does not press the panel. The panel is a rigid slab.

candidates.rating: rated 4.15 kg on a smooth face (holding force over a 1.5 safety factor)
candidates.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). The holding force is the sum of the sealed cups' caps; the payload is that force over a safety factor (1.5 smooth, 2.0 porous, 2.5 swivelling, all [assumed]) at 1 g. Only the smooth rating is a simulated claim: the porous and swivelling ratings are arithmetic on the same force, because no leak, porosity or swivel is simulated. Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

candidates.caveat: Nut runner (approximation): a rigid hex socket with a guide funnel on a lateral float; it engages a hex member by shape. The Studio wrist's roll is its spindle [assumed], at the wrist's speed: a clutch limits the torque to its cap (10 N m, under the wrist's 15 N m) and lets go at the release. tool_details.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

Suction cup (approximation): a compliant lip of rigid segments on a bellows spring with a limited tilt; the seal is a geometric test (every lip segment touching the face, part material under 13 rays inside the lip) gating a MuJoCo adhesion actuator capped at vacuum x lip area (at most 60 kPa). The lip must touch the face: no pull across a gap. Not modelled: air flow, leak rate, porosity, vacuum build-up time (the vacuum follows the shared close ramp and is cut the control tick the seal is lost), lip material hysteresis, peel dynamics beyond the contact distribution. The lip's friction is the part's. Treat suction results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

Suction cup (approximation): a compliant lip of rigid segments on a bellows spring with a limited tilt; the seal is a geometric test (every lip segment touching the face, part material under 13 rays inside the lip) gating a MuJoCo adhesion actuator capped at vacuum x lip area (at most 60 kPa). The lip must touch the face: no pull across a gap. Not modelled: air flow, leak rate, porosity, vacuum build-up time (the vacuum follows the shared close ramp and is cut the control tick the seal is lost), lip material hysteresis, peel dynamics beyond the contact distribution. The lip's friction is the part's. Treat suction results as a screen, then verify on hardware.
